key_insight: A coupled CFD-DDA framework shows that UV scattering inside saliva droplets is highly non-uniform and can materially change airborne virus inactivation predictions.
engineering_relevance: The model can improve the design and tuning of UV air-purification systems by accounting for droplet size, shape, airflow, evaporation, and wall interactions.
method: Couple a CFD Euler–Lagrange droplet transport/evaporation solver with a DDA light-scattering solver.
Simulate spherical and irregular saliva droplets under UV irradiation in 3D airflow.
Use DDA results to define the Dbouk-Yurkin law, extending Chick-Watson with scattering effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 3D coupled simulation study comparing droplet shapes, size distributions, airflow rates, and boundary interactions to predict surviving coronavirus copies Ns.
watch_item: The framework appears computationally intensive and depends on assumptions such as virion size, temperature, humidity, and droplet optical properties.
paper_title: An Innovative Computational Fluid Dynamics Discrete Dipole Approximation (CFD-DDA) Platform for Predicting Airborne Virus-in-Saliva Disinfection by Ultraviolet Irradiation
